headline: CATL'S JIANXIAWO EIA REVOKED — WORLD'S BIGGEST LITHIUM MINE BACK ON CARE AND MAINTENANCE; BENCHMARK CUTS 2026 SUPPLY FORECAST 49%
snippet: CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Sichuan — one of the world's largest hard-rock lithium operations — is back on care and maintenance after the Yichun Ecology and Environment Bureau withdrew the mine's Environmental Impact Assessment acceptance notice. The revocation followed more than 70 complaints lodged with regulators after CATL attempted to quietly resume mining in July while a tailings pond compliance dispute remained unresolved. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence immediately cut its 2026 mined output forecast for Jianxiawo to 32,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent from 62,500 tonnes — a 49% reduction — with the possibility that a full environmental review could stretch into 2027. The development is a significant supply-side shock for a lithium market that had priced in a gradual restart at Jianxiawo: with Core Lithium's Finniss restart only partially offsetting, and CATL's mine now off the production calendar, the 2026 structural deficit picture has tightened materially.

headline: STANMORE RESOURCES ACQUIRES MORANBAH SOUTH MET COAL FROM EXXARO FOR US$105M — 743MT RESOURCE IN QUEENSLAND'S BOWEN BASIN
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) has agreed to acquire the Moranbah South mine joint venture from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million in a deal announced September 5, expanding its footprint in Queensland's Bowen Basin — the world's premier metallurgical coal producing region. The Moranbah South tenements hold 743 million tonnes of coal resources, including 505 Mt indicated at 18.5% volatile matter and 219 Mt inferred. The transaction has a structured origin: Exxaro exercised its pre-emptive right under an existing joint venture agreement to first acquire Anglo American's 50% stake (triggered by Anglo's broader Australian coal asset divestment to Dhilmar QLD Ltd.), then immediately agreed to sell the resulting 100% interest to Stanmore. Subject to Australian regulatory approvals including transfer of mining rights, the deal is expected to close by year-end 2026. With metallurgical coal remaining essential to steelmaking in Asia's industrialising economies, the acquisition consolidates Stanmore's position as a growing independent met coal producer.

headline: ANGLO-TECK $53B MERGER AWAITS CHINESE ANTITRUST — CLOSE WINDOW SEPT 2026–MARCH 2027; $4.5B DIVIDEND FOLLOWS IN 45 DAYS
snippet: The Anglo American-Teck Resources merger of equals — the $53-billion all-stock transaction that would create one of the world's largest diversified copper miners — has cleared every regulatory hurdle except one: China's MOFCOM antitrust approval. Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad confirmed in July that active engagement with Chinese regulators is ongoing, and both companies are targeting a closing window between September 2026 and March 2027, with real tail risk on both sides of that range given China's unpredictable review timelines. On closing, Anglo American shareholders are entitled to a ~US$4.5 billion special dividend payable within 45 days. For junior copper investors, the merger signals how capital-constrained the world's largest copper producers have become relative to demand growth — no organic project can replicate the combined asset base, reinforcing the value of exploration-stage copper discoveries in stable jurisdictions.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES SUREBET: BONANZA AND GOLDEN GATE ZONES CONNECTED BY NEW WEDGE ZONES — GOLDEN TRIANGLE SYSTEM NOW 2.01 KM²
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSXV: GOT) confirmed August 31 that newly defined volcanic Wedge Zones — comprised of gold-bearing quartz-sulphide mineralization — directly connect the previously separate Bonanza and Golden Gate Zones at its 100%-owned Surebet Discovery in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Multiple drill holes intersect broad intervals of continuous gold mineralisation across the wedge corridor, including results up to 7.38 g/t gold equivalent over 35.7 metres. The confirmed connection significantly expands the known volume of the mineralised system, bringing the total mapped footprint to 2.01 square kilometres. The Golden Gate Zone alone has been expanded 480 metres to the northeast and 540 metres to the southwest during the 2026 season, with its footprint growing 38% to 1.17 km². The fully funded 50,000-metre, seven-rig program has 34,990 metres completed across 59 holes, with assays pending on multiple additional holes. With gold near $4,400/oz, a connected multi-zone discovery of this scale in a proven camp is a material re-rating event.

headline: BRIXTON METALS DRILLS 6,199 g/t SILVER AT LANGIS — HISTORIC COBALT CAMP RETURNS BONANZA GRADES INCLUDING 12,386 g/t OVER 0.5M; TSXV: BBB
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) reported September 2 that 33 new diamond drill holes at its wholly owned Langis Silver Project in Ontario's historic Cobalt silver camp have returned exceptional bonanza-grade silver intercepts. Best hole LM-26-432 from the Shaft 6 target zone returned 1.00 metre grading 6,199 g/t silver from 116.05 metres depth, including 0.50 metres at 12,386 g/t — the highest-grade intercept the company has reported at Langis. Earlier in the program, hole LM-26-399 returned a broad envelope of 41.00 metres at 79.2 g/t silver. To date in 2026, Brixton has completed 33,858 metres across 155 holes at Langis. The Cobalt silver camp in northeastern Ontario is one of North America's most historically prolific silver districts, characterized by high-grade native silver veins with extraordinary spot grades. With silver averaging ~$74/oz year-to-date — 116% above 2025 comparable levels — and a structural sixth-year supply deficit, the economics for developing a high-grade Cobalt silver deposit have never been more compelling.

headline: VULCAN ENERGY UNVEILS €1.26B PROJECT LUDWIG — SECOND GERMAN LITHIUM PFS DELIVERS $4.21B PRE-TAX NPV AND 25% IRR
snippet: Vulcan Energy Resources (ASX: VUL) released the prefeasibility study for Project Ludwig — its second lithium project in Germany's Upper Rhine Valley — on September 3, revealing economics that eclipse many conventional hard-rock lithium projects. The PFS outlines a pre-tax net present value of €2.6 billion (US$4.21 billion), an IRR of 25%, and annual production of 21,100 tonnes of battery-grade lithium carbonate over a 30-year operating life funded by €1.26 billion in development capital. Located approximately 60 kilometres north of Vulcan's flagship Lionheart project, Ludwig targets the same geothermal lithium brine extraction process — no tailings, no evaporation ponds, direct extraction of lithium from subsurface brines. Vulcan owns 85% of Project Ludwig with Siemens, Hochtief, and DemEA holding the balance; the company is launching a process to bring in additional strategic investors, with interest from both European and Asian parties. A final investment decision on Ludwig is contingent on Lionheart reaching commercial production, with the economic model assuming an FID in 2029.

headline: UTAH STATE BACKS ANSON RESOURCES' GREEN RIVER LITHIUM WITH $194M UIPA INCENTIVE OVER 25 YEARS — ASX: ASN
snippet: The Utah Inland Port Authority (UIPA) Board approved a US$194 million business incentive for A1 Lithium — Anson Resources' (ASX: ASN) Utah subsidiary — on September 3, 2026, supporting development of the Green River Lithium Project in Castle Country. The incentive is structured as 50% of the incremental property tax differential generated by the project for up to 25 years, delivering approximately US$8 million per year after commercial production begins, capped at the US$194 million total. The UIPA approval completes a broader ~US$358 million state incentive package that Anson received earlier in 2026, combining tax reimbursements and port authority revenue sharing over 20–25 years. Green River is a direct lithium extraction project targeting production from Utah's underground brine deposits — one of several US government-backed initiatives to build domestic critical mineral supply chains independent of China. The incentive significantly de-risks project economics and reduces the capital burden on equity investors.

headline: KAZATOMPROM SLASHES 2026 URANIUM GUIDANCE 10% — COMBINED WITH CAMECO MCARTHUR RIVER CONSTRAINTS, STRUCTURAL DEFICIT DEEPENS
snippet: Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer supplying roughly 43% of global mine output, cut its 2026 production guidance by approximately 10%, setting output at 27,500–29,000 tonnes of uranium (71.5–75.4 million pounds U3O8) on a 100% basis — versus earlier indications of approximately 77 million pounds. The reduction reflects continued delays at the TQZ sulphuric acid plant and broader well-field development constraints in Kazakhstan. Simultaneously, Cameco has guided McArthur River/Key Lake production at 14–16.5 million pounds for 2026, down from original targets, due to mining area development delays at the world's highest-grade uranium mine. The simultaneous downside guidance from the two most consequential uranium suppliers represents a material supply tightening in a market where reactor demand is growing structurally: the World Nuclear Association's latest forecast projects global reactor requirements to more than double by 2040, driven by SMR commercialisation, life extensions, and new-build programmes in the US, Japan, South Korea, and Europe.

headline: URANIUM JUNIOR MINERS SURGE 21.75% IN AUGUST — SPROTT DOCUMENTS CONVICTION BUYING AS WNA DOUBLES DEMAND FORECAST TO 2040
snippet: Sprott's September 2026 uranium report documents a remarkably strong August for the nuclear fuel complex: the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index gained 17.01% on the month while junior uranium miners surged 21.75%, outpacing every major equity sector and commodity benchmark. Spot uranium rebounded to approximately $82–89/lb range in August, recovering from a mid-year dip, driven by utility demand for term contracts and acute awareness of supply constraints at Kazatomprom and Cameco. Sprott characterises the buying as institutional 'conviction' — not momentum — supported by the World Nuclear Association's projection that global reactor requirements will more than double by 2040 as data-centre power demand, SMR commercialisation, and decarbonisation commitments drive a sustained expansion of nuclear capacity. Microsoft's long-term nuclear power purchase agreements and the UK's new small modular reactor programme have attracted fresh attention from generalist institutional capital that sat out the 2023–2024 uranium cycle.

headline: BRIEN LUNDIN: US TREASURY BOND BUYBACKS SIGNAL GOLD IS ENTERING A NEW DEBASEMENT PHASE — MINERS STILL PRICED FOR GOLD AT $2,500
snippet: Brien Lundin, editor of Gold Newsletter and host of the New Orleans Investment Conference, argues in his most recent K E Report interview that the US Treasury's August announcement of its first steps toward Yield Curve Control — buying back long-duration Treasury bonds to manage the yield curve — represents the single most consequential structural development for gold in 2026. Lundin frames it plainly: 'Unless aliens land and give us the secret to limitless power and interstellar travel, we're not going to grow our way out of the debt.' The debt-debasement trade is no longer a fringe thesis — institutional investors are now building positions explicitly against fiscal deterioration, which Lundin argues is why gold has continued rising despite a 60% FOMC rate-hike probability. Most importantly for junior mining investors, Lundin notes that major gold mining stocks remain priced as if gold were at $2,500, not $4,400: the re-rating from P/NAV compression to fair-value recovery has barely begun, and high-beta juniors with proven resources offer the greatest leverage to the next leg.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO RISES TO 67:1 AS SILVER CORRECTS FROM $121 JANUARY PEAK — SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT YEAR, JPM TARGETS $85 IN Q4
snippet: The gold-silver ratio has climbed to approximately 67:1 in September 2026, up from a cycle low of 45.6:1 in January when silver briefly touched $121 per ounce. Silver has since corrected to the mid-$70s range, averaging $73–74 year-to-date — still 116.7% above the 2025 comparable period. The ratio's rise to 67:1 sits in a neutral historical zone: readings above 80:1 have historically signalled silver as deeply undervalued relative to gold, while readings below 50:1 have marked gold as cheap relative to silver. The Silver Institute projects a 67-million-ounce supply deficit in 2026 — the sixth consecutive year of structural undersupply — driven by booming industrial demand for solar panels, EVs, and AI data-centre UPS systems. J.P. Morgan has set a Q4 2026 price target of $85 per ounce for silver, implying a Q4 ratio of roughly 52:1 at current gold levels. For retail investors, the ratio's current 67:1 reading provides a disciplined, historically grounded entry-point framework for adding silver exposure ahead of a potential second-half ratio compression.
